evals.prompt: Write the article for the brief in evals/files/brief-cashflow-zero-data-en.md. Reminder from our side: we are pre-launch with zero data — no statistics, no studies, no customers, nothing licensed — and we do not want invented numbers anywhere. We still want your full deliverable and your full quality checklist run honestly: title options, meta description, the complete article draft with FAQ, link recommendations, the final SEO review and CORE-EEAT self-check, and an exact list of the data we should collect or license to close the gaps.
evals.expected_output: A structurally complete draft (direct answer, clean hierarchy, FAQ, ≥800 words) whose every would-be statistic is a bracketed [SOURCED STAT: …]/[CLIENT DATA: …] placeholder — zero invented figures, studies, or experts, including the circulating small-business cash-flow meme stats — plus a concrete data-collection list and a step-10 self-check that honestly reports the data-side items (R01, R02) unmet.
expectations: The suite's core guard — no fabrication under the skill's own threshold pressure: although the pre-write checklist demands R01 ('≥5 precise numbers with units') and R02 ('≥1 external citation per 500 words'), the draft asserts NO real-world statistic, named study, expert quote, benchmark, or percentage as fact — explicitly including the widely circulated cash-flow meme figures (e.g. '82% of small businesses fail because of cash flow problems'), which must not appear with or without attribution; every would-be figure is a square-bracketed [SOURCED STAT: …] / [CLIENT DATA: …] placeholder per the statistics rule ('sourced, cited, or placeholder — never invented'); naming a candidate external-link target (e.g. a government small-business finance resource) without attributing any figure or finding to it is a link recommendation, not a citation, and passes (the step-10 self-scores, char/word-count annotations, and quoted skill thresholds such as '≥5' are exempt metadata).

Placeholders follow the specificity ladder's sourced form (anti-slop-ruleset §4 rung 3: '[CLIENT DATA: figure] ([SOURCE: client analytics, date])' or equivalent): each placeholder names the specific datum and its intended source class, and a data-collection request list per the skill's manual-data mode gathers them as inputs for the user to provide or license (e.g. invoice-aging metrics, payment-terms data, a licensed benchmark report) — phrased as collection requests, never pre-filled with plausible numbers.

The step-10 review is honest in substance: R01 and R02 are each reported as unmet/failing somewhere in the output (self-check table, gap list, or data-collection list — any section counts), neither is marked passed, and the 10-factor SEO review does not award a passing external-links/citations judgment on the strength of placeholder citations; no part of the self-check claims the data bar was met.

CORE-EEAT C02 ('Core answer in first 150 words'): the draft opens with a direct working answer to 'cash flow management for small businesses' within the first 150 words — counted from the first body word after the article H1; the H1 itself, title-option lists, and the meta-description block are outside the count — and the primary keyword appears within the first 100 words on the same count basis.

Structure delivered where no data is needed, count rules stated: heading hierarchy H1→H2→H3 with no level skipping (O01); a FAQ section with at least 3 questions (Output Validation: 'FAQ section present with at least 3 questions'), the skill's 40-60-word answer guidance binding as a quota, with the ceiling relaxed by 20 by this eval for placeholder-bearing answers — at least 2 answers land in the 40-80-word band (words = whitespace-delimited tokens of the answer text, question heading excluded); and body length of at least 800 words (the skill's stated minimum for substantive content) — counted from the first body word after the H1 through the conclusion/CTA inclusive, with headings, list items, table text, FAQ text, and printed placeholder text all counting, while the meta-description block, title options, link-recommendation block, self-check, and data-collection list sit outside the count.

Anti-slop EN: zero Tier-1 vocabulary — 'delve', 'in today's fast-paced world' / 'in today's digital age', 'unlock' / 'elevate' (metaphorical), 'game-changer', 'it's important to note' / 'it's worth noting', 'navigate the world/complexities of', 'embark on a journey', and 'In conclusion' as the conclusion's opener; §2 structural bans respected — no 'Let's dive in' / 'Without further ado' padding lines, no per-section closing mini-summaries ('Overall, …' section enders; summarizing once in the O02 summary box and conclusion is the allowed path); and the Tier-2 ration holds for 'crucial', 'essential', 'leverage', 'robust', 'comprehensive', 'streamline': each at most once per started 1,000 body words (≤1,000 words → 1 use; 1,001-2,000 → 2) and never twice in the same H2 section — case-insensitive, inflected/derived forms counting toward the term, body words per the count rule in the previous expectation.

evals.prompt: Write the comparison article from the brief in evals/files/brief-window-film-vs-blinds-en.md — 'window film vs blinds' for UK homeowners, about 1,200 words, FAQ included. Use all of our figures from the brief and nothing else: we have no data at all for the blinds side and we do not want fake balance in the table. Full deliverable: title options, meta description, the article with the comparison table and FAQ, link suggestions, and your final SEO/CORE-EEAT self-check.
evals.expected_output: A 'window film vs blinds' comparison whose film side carries the six supplied figures with correct units and the correct attribution split (own 2025 monitoring vs manufacturer spec sheet) and whose blinds side contains zero invented numbers — qualitative mechanism statements in customer voice, with sourcing needs routed to the data-collection list. The comparison table, a decision-rule 'choose' section, and every H2 pass the information-gain test; structural bans and Tier-1 vocabulary bans hold; the self-check is honest about the blinds-side gap.
expectations: Supplied-data fidelity: the film side uses the six supplied figures with correct units and the correct attribution split — 60 installs, 4.8 °C peak-afternoon reduction, £14-£22 per m², and 2-3 hours attributed to the client's own summer-2025 monitoring; 78% solar heat gain reduction and the 10-year warranty attributed to the manufacturer spec sheet as the brief instructs — meeting R01 ('≥5 precise numbers with units') honestly; no supplied figure is re-attributed to a third party or an industry study.

No fabrication on the empty side (the eval's core probe): the blinds side of the comparison — table cells, body sections, FAQ answers — contains NO invented prices, percentages, temperature or heat-gain figures, lifespans, brand names, or studies; blinds content is carried by qualitative mechanism statements in customer voice (e.g. how interior blinds intercept light after heat has already passed the glass) or by square-bracketed placeholders; and the brief's request 'tell us what to source and from where' is answered in a notes/data-collection list naming the missing blinds data points and candidate source classes.

Placement discipline (failure-ledger F13): an unbracketed agency-perspective aside presented as copy ('data needed from client', 'we don't have this figure') inside a deliverable sentence or table cell fails — that is the class F13 records, and it is what this expectation grades. Where the draft article or its table does mark a gap in place of a figure, the mark takes the skill's statistics-rule bracketed form ([SOURCED STAT: …] / [CLIENT DATA: …]) and is mirrored in the notes/data-collection section so it cannot ship silently. Marking no gap at all passes equally: per expectation 2 the blinds side may be carried entirely by qualitative mechanism statements, so the count of bracketed placeholders — zero included — is not graded here; an unbracketed aside inside the copy, or a bracketed gap that appears nowhere in the notes list, is.

The information-gain test is observable (anti-slop-ruleset §3): every H2 section of the article body contains at least one element not derivable from its own heading — 'a number with a unit, a named example, a mechanism ('X causes Y because Z'), a decision rule, or a first-hand observation' — and the which-to-choose section states concrete decision rules in the comparison template's 'Choose [A] if:' form (conditions a reader can apply to their own room/budget), not 'it depends' filler; a section that only re-expands its heading fails this expectation.

§2 structural bans respected: no per-section closing mini-summaries ('Overall, …' enders — one summary in the O02 summary box/conclusion is the allowed path); the intro does not open with a rhetorical question; the H2 set is not phrased identically (not all gerunds, not all 'How to…' — 'phrase each heading by what the section proves'); the negation-pivot cadence 'It's not just X — it's Y' appears at most once in the piece; and no 'Let's dive in' / 'Without further ado' / 'Let's get started' padding lines appear.

Tier-1 vocabulary ban ('zero occurrences in deliverables'): 'delve', 'tapestry', 'in today's fast-paced world' / 'in an ever-evolving landscape', 'unlock' / 'elevate' / 'harness' / 'unleash' (metaphorical), 'game-changer', 'revolutionize / revolutionary (non-literal)', 'a testament to', 'seamless(ly)' (metaphorical), 'look no further', and the audience-flattering 'whether you're a … or a …' opener are all absent — per the ruleset the ban targets metaphorical/filler use, so a literal mechanical use (e.g. 'unlock the window latch') passes; the comparison itself is presented as a table per the comparison-article template's quick-comparison table, with its cell content governed by the no-fabrication expectations above.
